Density Underlying the TOST Power Calculation

Source: R/power_equivalence_md.R
power_density_equivalence_md.Rd

Evaluates the integrand whose integral over \((0, \mathrm{upper})\) yields the power of the Schuirmann (1987) two one-sided tests procedure; see power_equivalence_md. Useful for plotting the integrand and for diagnostic work.

Usage

power_density_equivalence_md(
  sd_values,
  alpha_level,
  lower_bound,
  upper_bound,
  true_effect,
  true_sd,
  n_per_treatment,
  df_error
)

Arguments

sd_values

Numeric vector of \(\sigma\) values at which to evaluate the integrand.

alpha_level

Type I error rate for each of the two one-sided tests.

lower_bound

Lower limit of the equivalence interval on the analysis scale: a difference, or the logarithm of a ratio.

upper_bound

Upper limit of the equivalence interval on the analysis scale: a difference, or the logarithm of a ratio.

true_effect

The true (population) effect on the analysis scale: the difference in treatment means, or the logarithm of their ratio.

true_sd

\(\sqrt{\mathrm{error\ variance}}\).

n_per_treatment

Number of subjects who receive each treatment (the size of each group in a parallel design; every subject in a crossover design), as in power_equivalence_md.

df_error

Error degrees of freedom for true_sd.

Value

A data.frame with one row per supplied sd_values, and columns sd_values and power_density.

Details

The analysis scale. Unlike power_equivalence_md, which takes the bounds and the true effect on the original scale and logs ratios when logscale = TRUE, this function has no logscale argument and transforms nothing: lower_bound, upper_bound, and true_effect are on the scale of the analysis, differences of the means, or, for means compared on the log scale, logarithms of the ratios (log(0.8) for a ratio of 0.8).

Note

See the legacy MBESS package (Kelley, 2007a, 2007b) for additional details and discussion.

References

Kelley, K. (2007a). Confidence intervals for standardized effect sizes: Theory, application, and implementation. Journal of Statistical Software, 20(8), 1–24. doi:10.18637/jss.v020.i08

Kelley, K. (2007b). Methods for the behavioral, educational, and social sciences: An R package. Behavior Research Methods, 39(4), 979–984. doi:10.3758/BF03192993

Phillips, K. F. (1990). Power of the two one-sided tests procedure in bioequivalence. Journal of Pharmacokinetics and Biopharmaceutics, 18(2), 137–144. doi:10.1007/BF01063556

Schuirmann, D. J. (1987). A comparison of the two one-sided tests procedure and the power approach for assessing the equivalence of average bioavailability. Journal of Pharmacokinetics and Biopharmaceutics, 15(6), 657–680.

See also

power_equivalence_md, power_equivalence_md_plot

Other equivalence testing: equivalence_c(), equivalence_proportion_paired(), equivalence_r(), equivalence_rmsea(), equivalence_smd(), plot_equivalence(), power_equivalence_c(), power_equivalence_md(), power_equivalence_md_plot(), ss_power_equivalence_c()

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

# Density at a single value of true_sd:
power_density_equivalence_md(sd_values = 0.10, alpha_level = .05,
                             lower_bound = -.2, upper_bound = .2,
                             true_effect = .05, true_sd = .20,
                             n_per_treatment = 24, df_error = 22)
#>   sd_values power_density
#> 1       0.1    0.02297896

# Vectorized over a grid:
grid <- power_density_equivalence_md(
  sd_values = seq(0.01, 0.40, length.out = 50),
  alpha_level = .05, lower_bound = -.2, upper_bound = .2,
  true_effect = .05, true_sd = .20, n_per_treatment = 24, df_error = 22
)
head(grid)
#>    sd_values power_density
#> 1 0.01000000  3.625481e-22
#> 2 0.01795918  7.451634e-17
#> 3 0.02591837  1.498398e-13
#> 4 0.03387755  3.634158e-11
#> 5 0.04183673  2.582758e-09
#> 6 0.04979592  8.170958e-08

# On the log scale the bounds and the true effect are logarithms of the
# ratios: the ratios .8, 1.25, and 1.05 of power_equivalence_md(logscale =
# TRUE) are given here as their logarithms.
power_density_equivalence_md(sd_values = 0.10, alpha_level = .05,
                             lower_bound = log(.8), upper_bound = log(1.25),
                             true_effect = log(1.05), true_sd = .20,
                             n_per_treatment = 18, df_error = 16)
#>   sd_values power_density
#> 1       0.1     0.1317922
